title: Finite Tor amplitude at field coefficients
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $F$ and $K$ be at a field coefficient stage: either $F=E$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,E)$ in the raw rationalized category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], or $F=\Qlb$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ in the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with the coefficient datum of those definitions. Then $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,F)$, with this field-stage subcategory defined in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For the ordinary constant-coefficient meaning of the tensor-vanishing assertion, let $K_F=J_F(K)\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},F)$ be the explicitly specified realization of [lem-sf-field-stage-ordinary-realization], and let $F_Y$ be the discrete constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then $K_F$ has finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]: there are integers $a\le b$ such that, for every sheaf $M$ of $F_Y$-modules placed in degree zero,
$$\mathcal H^r(K_F\otimes^L_{F_Y}M)=0\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b]).$$
Here the tensor product is the ordinary derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor] and $\mathcal H^r$ is the cohomology sheaf of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

proof.text: At field stages [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] defines $D^b_{ctf}(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,E)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Qlb)=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$. Thus the assumed membership of $K$ in the appropriate bounded constructible field-stage category is exactly its membership in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,F)$.

source.place: Proof, field-flatness computation and boundedness sentence, with the ordinary realization made explicit

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-field-stage-ordinary-realization] to the given field-stage object. It supplies the well-defined ordinary object $K_F=J_F(K)$ and its cohomological boundedness, including when $K$ is represented by a finite-stage pair $(E,C)$ at $F=\Qlb$. Choose integers $a\le b$ such that $\mathcal H^r(K_F)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. The choice concerns $K_F$ alone and precedes any choice of the test sheaf $M$.

source.place: Proof, field-flatness computation and boundedness sentence, with the ordinary realization made explicit

proof.text: Fix any representative L of the realized object K_F, any quasi-isomorphism f:P→L with P K-flat, and any degree-zero module sheaf M, as quantified by def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude. The derived homology comparison and f identify H^i(P) with H^i(K_F). Apply lem-exc-constant-field-sheaf-tensor-cohomology to P and M over the lifted constant field. Outside the interval from Step 2 its source H^i(P) tensor M is zero. The localization tensor and the sectionwise sheafified tensor are naturally isomorphic (compose the sheafification counit isomorphism, functorial right tensoring, the monoidal sheafification comparison, and the sectionwise presheaf tensor isomorphism; each is natural). The single-factor total-tensor comparison identifies P tensor M[0] with this termwise tensor. Finally the standard derived homology comparison gives the vanishing in def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude. This proves every quantified resolution test directly; no new K-flat resolution is chosen.
